title: Logical Reasoning
description: Class 11 IMO — Logical Reasoning: number and letter series, analogy and coding–decoding, direction and blood relations, and cubes, calendars, clocks and data sufficiency.

topics.title: Series, Analogy and Coding–Decoding
topics.concept: In a series, find the rule (difference, ratio, squares, alternation) and extend it. Analogy and classification test a shared pattern; in coding–decoding work out the letter or digit shift from the example and apply it.

examples.solution: Gaps 4, 6, 8 grow by 2, so the next gap is 10 → 30.

recap: Series: spot the rule and extend.
Coding: find the shift from the example, then apply.

quiz.q: If p is true and q is false, then ¬(p ∨ q) is:
quiz.explanation: p ∨ q is true, so its negation is false.

quiz.q: If p: '5 is odd' and q: '8 is even', then p ∧ q is:
quiz.explanation: Both p and q are true, so p ∧ q is true.

topics.title: Direction, Distance and Blood Relations
topics.concept: Direction problems track turns; the straight-line distance comes from Pythagoras. Blood relations are solved by sketching a family tree from the clues.

examples.problem: 3 km east then 4 km north — distance from start?
A's mother is B's sister — B is A's?

recap: Draw a family tree for blood relations.

quiz.explanation: Parabolas of form x² = 4ay are symmetric about the y-axis.

quiz.q: If f(x) = 5x + 3 for x ≤ 1, and f(x) = 2x² + k for x > 1, find k so that lim(x→1) f(x) exists.
quiz.explanation: For the limit to exist, LHL = RHL at x = 1. LHL = 5(1) + 3 = 8. RHL = 2(1)² + k = 2 + k. Equating them: 2 + k = 8 → k = 6.

topics.title: Cubes, Calendars, Clocks and Data Sufficiency
topics.concept: On a standard die opposite faces total 7. The clock minute hand turns 6°/min and the hour hand 0.5°/min. Data sufficiency asks whether the statements are enough — not the answer itself.

examples.problem: A die shows 2 on top — bottom face?

recap: Data sufficiency judges adequacy, not the value.

quiz.q: Which measure is most affected by extreme values?
quiz.explanation: Mean uses every observation and is sensitive to outliers.

questions.q: The locus of a point for which y = 0 and z = 0 is:
questions.explanation: When both y and z coordinates are zero, the x-coordinate can be any real number. This is the exact definition of the x-axis.

questions.q: What is the focal distance of a point (x₁, y₁) on the parabola x² = -4ay?
questions.explanation: For x² = -4ay, focus is (0, -a) and directrix is y = a. By definition, focal distance equals distance to directrix. Distance from (x₁, y₁) to y = a is |y₁ - a|.

questions.q: If A and B are equal sets, then:
Which among the strictly matched pairing of spatial points reliably confirms their existence identically within the same absolute geometric octant?
questions.explanation: Points sharing an octant practically display universally identical sign signatures. Evaluating strictly: (2, 3, −4) yields (+, +, −). Similarly, (5, 1, −2) delivers identically (+, +, −). Both firmly inhabit Octant V.

questions.q: For any two sets A and B, the Commutative Law for union states that:
questions.explanation: The Commutative Law implies that the order of sets does not change the result of the operation. So, A ∪ B = B ∪ A.

questions.q: The compound statement (p → q) ∧ (q → p) is logically equivalent to:
questions.explanation: The biconditional statement 'p if and only if q' strictly means 'if p then q' AND 'if q then p'.

questions.q: If statement p is true, then the statement p ∨ ~p is a:
questions.explanation: p ∨ ~p means 'True OR False', which always evaluates to True. A statement that is always true is called a tautology.

questions.q: For a point P on the ellipse x²/49 + y²/25 = 1, find the sum of its focal distances.
questions.explanation: Sum of focal distances = 2a. Here a²=49 => a=7. Sum = 2(7) = 14.

questions.q: Which of the following sets are disjoint?
Which among the strictly following defined spatial points sits nearest to the absolute spatial origin (0, 0, 0)?
questions.explanation: Compare the squared absolute distances: A is 4+4+1 = 9. B is 9. C is 1+1+1 = 3. D is 0+4+4 = 8. The smallest squared distance is 3, proving (1, 1, 1) is absolutely closest.
